text.p: Kimball International Inc said Tuesday that Douglas Habig, president and chief executive officer, will become chairman of the company effective July 1.
Douglas Habig, 50, takes over as chairman from his brother, Thomas Habig, 69, who will become vice chairman of the board.
Douglas Habig will remain as chief executive.
James Thyen, 53, will become president. Thyen mostly recently served as senior executive vice president, chief financial and administrative officer, and treasurer.

Gary Critser remains senior executive vice president and secretary and adds the additional title of treasurer. Robert Schneider, vice president and director of accounting, will become executive vice president, chief financial officer and assistant treasurer.

"We have taken the steps to help ensure Kimball's continued success and positioning for healthy growth," Douglas Habig said in a statement. "These appointments are the result of a management succession plan that has been in place for some time. It is intended to allow the company to move ahead aggressively as we address the challenges of the next 10 years and beyond."
Kimball is a diversified manufacturer of consumer durable goods, including office, residential, hospitality and health care furniture.
